MEETING HEADER:
Date: 2027-07-13
Start: 10:00 AM PT
Duration: ~55 minutes
Attendees: Jordan Lee, Priya Nair, Ethan Ramos (Redwood); Marta Gomez, Liam O'Connor, Aisha Khan (Northbridge Health)
Artifacts shared: se_enablement_deck_v3.pdf, competitive_battlecard_link (internal), demo-recording-link (to be uploaded)

SUMMARY (auto-gen, may be rough):
Quick messaging refresher and live demo practice focused on enterprise objections: latency vs cost, dedicated vs hosted, data residency and SOC2. Practiced two demo flows: "Support Triage" and "Clinical Note Summarization". Collected feedback and ownership for follow-ups.

TRANSCRIPT:
[00:00] Jordan: hey everyone, thanks for joining. we got about 55 minutes today to run through messaging and do a quick demo practice. Priya and Ethan are gonna role-play the demo pieces. Marta, Liam, Aisha from Northbridge, thank you for making time.
[00:18] Marta: yeah thanks Jordan, excited to see this — we're trying to align internal teams on how we'd talk about inference costs and also how a POC would work.
[00:28] Priya: cool, quick agenda: 1) core positioning refresh, 2) competitive notes, 3) demo run through two flows, 4) feedback & next steps. Sound good?
[00:37] Liam: yep that's perfect. our timeline is tight, Q3 ideally.
[00:41] Ethan: quick lane on language — we sometimes call Redwood services slightly different in docs, like "Redwood Dedicate" in one place, so we'll try to keep consistent: Redwood API (hosted), Redwood Dedicated (reserved GPU pools), Redwood Private (VPC/on-prem).
[00:58] Jordan: nice callout. messaging nugget: "We make inference predictable and economical across environments" — that's the one-liner. Emphasize production levers: batching, KV/prefix caching, quantization profiles.
[01:12] Marta: could you unpack KV a bit? we've got engineers who are fuzzy on that term.
[01:19] Priya: sure — KV cache means we store previous key/value states for transformer decoders so repeated prefixes or chat contexts don't recompute the full sequence — big wins on per token compute. it's automatic for many workloads.
[01:33] Aisha: how does that interact with sessions where privacy rules force not storing any context?
[01:38] Ethan: good question — we can disable caching, or use in-memory ephemeral cache that doesn't persist to disk; for Private/VPC deployments you can control retention and KMS for keys. we also have an HSM option for certain enterprise customers.
[01:54] Marta: ok good. can you talk tradeoffs between hosted and dedicated for us? cost/perf wise?
[02:01] Jordan: sure. hosted API is lowest friction, great for dev + early prod; dedicated is reserved capacity for predictable latency and throughput — you commit capacity, we pre-allocate GPU pools, autoscale policies are configurable. generally dedicated yields lower tail latency and better isolation but at commit costs.
[02:20] Liam: do you have example unit economics? like tokens per second, cost per 1M tokens?
[02:27] Priya: we usually share region/model specific numbers — for example, a quantized Llama-like variant on a common GPU can do X tokens/s, and batching + KV often reduces effective cost by 30-50% depending on prompt distribution. we'll follow up with a spreadsheet.
[02:44] Jordan: yep sending benchmark sheet after call — it'll have Bedrock comparisons and our numbers.
[02:49] Marta: speaking of Bedrock, how do you position vs Bedrock and Anthropic on security and enterprise controls?
[02:57] Ethan: Bedrock is fine for managed models but it's tied to AWS control plane and RBAC; Redwood differentiator is unified runtime across hosted/dedicated/private and explicit audit logs, KMS integration and SOC2/ISO-ready artifacts. Anthropic tends to be strong on model safety but less focused on deployment ops.
[03:17] Jordan: important to mention: for regulated customers, we offer Private with customer-managed networking and optional on-prem bundle. that's often the clincher.
[03:26] Liam: great — let's move to the demo.

DEMO PRACTICE (Support Triage flow)
[03:33] Priya: ok I'll demo a quick support triage where the app ingests a support thread and produces severity, suggested SLA and the action items. starting the sandbox… (screen share noise) 
[03:50] [sound of typing, faint background] Priya: here's the prompt: "Summarize issue, classify severity (low/med/high/critical), provide next steps and list config changes if needed."
[04:03] Priya: model returns: "High — multiple prod users impacted, suggested rollback, notify infra, open ticket for hotfix". pause — this is where we highlight deterministic outputs and reranking options.
[04:18] Marta: how do you show latency on stage?
[04:21] Ethan: we have a token-level latency gauge in the demo console; during hosted mode it shows median/95th. note sometimes the demo env is noisy; mention expected numbers rather than exact.
[04:34] Priya: (to Jordan) you want me to call out batching and cache savings here?
[04:37] Jordan: yes: "note — this request uses prefix caching because similar threads have been seen before, saving about 40% CPU cost in the demo env".
[04:45] Priya: got it. also quick glitch: the summarizer sometimes outputs 'prob' instead of 'problem' in the transcript — small transcription artifact, we can ignore.

DEMO PRACTICE (Clinical Note Summarization flow)
[04:55] Ethan: next flow, clinical note summarization: ingest raw clinician notes, output SOAP-style summary, flag PHI. starting sequence.
[05:08] Ethan: show model config: pinned model version, temperature 0.0 for determinism, quantization profile x4, and KMS enabled for attachments.
[05:20] Marta: PHI handling is critical — can you demo redaction?
[05:24] Priya: yes we toggle pii-redact which masks names and personal identifiers before sending to model, we can also keep redaction local in Private deployment.
[05:36] Aisha: curious about audit logs: if a clinician requests notes be deleted, how do you prove it was removed?
[05:42] Jordan: we keep immutable audit trails for model calls in the control plane and you can configure retention. for private installs logs can be routed to customer SIEM.

FEEDBACK & COMPETITIVE MESSAGING
[05:55] Marta: quick feedback — liked the one-liner, but the "predictable and economical" bit could be more concrete for execs, maybe add an example ROI sentence.
[06:03] Jordan: good — e.g., "30% lower unit cost on chat use cases with batching & KV vs vendor baseline" — we can add a slide with a small ROI calc.
[06:12] Liam: on competitive deck, call out where Bedrock forces you into AWS network egress and how that affects multi-cloud customers.
[06:19] Ethan: yes and add a note on model variants: we auto-fallback to cheaper variants when latency SLO is strict — useful talking point.
[06:28] Priya: role-play note — when customer asks cost vs latency, use the "three-lane" framework: dev/test (hosted), steady-prod (dedicated), regulated (private) and pick levers accordingly.

OBJECTIONS ROLE-PLAY
[06:40] Marta (role-play): "We already have Bedrock — why switch?"
[06:44] Jordan: reply: "Bedrock is convenient, but if you need predictable latency, cross-region routing, and consistent instrumentation across environments, Redwood reduces ops burden and gives transparent unit economics."
[06:56] Marta: nice, also mention audit logs and KMS quickly.
[07:00] Jordan: yep.

WRAP & NEXT STEPS
[07:04] Jordan: quick recap: we'll send the demo recording, updated battlecard, benchmark spreadsheet, and set a follow-up to scope a small POC if Northbridge is interested.
[07:13] Marta: sounds good. one ask — can you include a simple checklist for what we need from our infra team to start the POC? network, service account, expected token volumes, etc.
[07:22] Ethan: yes we'll include that as the POC checklist.
[07:26] Priya: final comment for SEs — when demoing, avoid overusing model internals jargon; keep customer-level benefits front and center (latency, cost, isolation).
[07:36] Jordan: perfect. thanks everyone. we'll follow up with links and owners as listed.
[07:42] Marta: thanks all.

END OF TRANSCRIPT
